text:
devon: FYI getting customer report that p99 for /v1/generate shot up to ~18s from baseline ~600ms starting ~00:30 UTC. Customer on Dedicated pool 'dp-east-12'. They hit a hard spike and saw several 504s. Escalating.

maria: thanks — are they on pinned model version or auto-routing?

devon: pinned to rwd-1.2.3-quantized, dedicated pool only. No fallback to hosted.

jordan: pinging runtime. i'm seeing a large backlog in attach queue for dp-east-12 around 00:28–00:35 UTC; attach latencies spiked to 12–20s. Looks like cold GPU start + container init.

autoscale-bot: [00:29:12] pool dp-east-12: desired=24, available=24, attaching=6, provisioning=0, warm=0
autoscale-bot: [00:30:05] pool dp-east-12: attach_latency_p95=12.4s, attach_latency_p99=18.7s

ashley: customer says they had a burst of traffic (20x typical qps) at 00:27 UTC. SLA says dedicated should handle predictable bursts but they didn't configure burst capacity.

maria: can we confirm whether warm pool is enabled for that pool? IIRC some older pools don't have warm nodes by default.

jordan: checking pool config: `warm_pool_enabled=false`, `min_nodes=4`, `max_nodes=48`, `attach_timeout=30s`. Looks like min_nodes too low for burst.

devon: can we do emergency mitigation: 1) temporarily bump min_nodes 2) enable fallback routing to hosted small variant 3) warm up a few GPUs manually?

jordan: I can bump min_nodes to 12 now. Running command: ```infractl pool update --pool dp-east-12 --min-nodes 12```
jordan: done — API returned 202. autoscale controller starting additional attaches.

autoscale-bot: [00:41:02] pool dp-east-12: desired=36, available=24, attaching=12

maria: pls also add a routing fallback rule for this customer's route so requests can go to hosted if attach latency > 5s. we'll need support approval for cross-tenant fallback.

ashley: I've informed the customer we enabled temporary capacity bump and suggested they enable fallback on their side. They want a postmortem.

jordan: quick note: initial root cause looks like a couple of issues colliding — 1) no warm pool so attaches require full cold init 2) attach controller was rate-limited because our attach token bucket was exhausted (we had a throttling bump due to an unrelated rollout last week) 3) customer burst > max instantaneous attach throughput.
maria: can you share the attach controller logs/snips?
jordan: paste logs: ```
[2026-02-11T00:29:10Z] attach-controller dp-east-12 attach_request accepted id=abc123
[2026-02-11T00:29:11Z] scheduler: enqueue attach id=abc123
[2026-02-11T00:29:22Z] attach-controller ERROR rate_limited: token-bucket empty
[2026-02-11T00:29:35Z] worker-7 init-gpu: pull-image (3.1s), load-checkpoint (6.8s), readiness-probe (1.6s)
[2026-02-11T00:29:41Z] attach-controller attach_complete id=abc123 latency=17.4s
```

maria: that rate limit + cold init explains p99 spikes. action items: disable rollout throttling (rollback config), increase attach token-bucket burst, enable warm_pool for pools handling customer bursts, recommend customers enable hosted fallback or reserved burst.

ashley: logging: recording customer impact and ETA for followup. Customer wants root-cause and mitigations.

jordan: I'm rolling a fast patch to attach-controller to surface throttling metrics and to avoid global token exhaustion across pools (scoping tokens per-pool). will open PR and backfill test.

maria: ops-runbook-bot, create incident page for DP attach surge?

ops-runbook-bot: incident created: https://redwood.ops/incidents/INC-2026-0311-attach-surge-dp-east-12 (assigned to eng-sre)

maria: followups (short):
- short-term (now): raised min_nodes -> decreased attach backlog, enabled emergency fallback rule for the customer, rollback rollout-throttle. assigned jordan + devon.
- mid-term (24–72h): enable warm_pool on pools that advertise burst capability, increase attach token-bucket default burst to 3x, add per-pool attach token scoping. assigned runtime team (jordan).
- long-term: autoscaler improvement: pre-warm heuristics based on burst history and traffic shape, customer-facing docs on recommended Dedicated config (warm_pool, min_nodes, burst capacity). assigned product + devex.

devon: repro steps for postmortem — to reproduce locally/onstaging:
1) create dedicated pool with `warm_pool_enabled=false`, `min_nodes=2`, `max_nodes=48`
2) pin a model that triggers full checkpoint load (rwd-1.2.3-quantized)
3) fire a traffic spike: 20 qps sustained for 90s using `wrk` script — attach ops should be saturated
4) watch attach-controller metrics `attach_latency_p95/p99`, token-bucket fill level, and pod init durations

jordan: added those steps to the incident page and attached a small `wrk` script snippet: ```
#!/bin/bash
wrk -t12 -c100 -d90s -s post.lua https://dedicated.example/v1/generate
```

maria: good. please include the config diff and timeline in the postmortem. Also propose a customer communication template for support.

ashley: drafting customer note: short apology, explanation of dedicated config limits, steps we took (min_nodes bump, enabled fallback), ETA for permanent fixes, offer temporary credits. will share draft in #support after ops review. :white_check_mark:

jordan: monitoring update: p95 now ~1.1s, p99 ~2.4s after min_nodes bump + some warm attach completes. We'll keep an eye for 24h.

devon: closing loop — thanks all. we'll schedule retro with product to cover docs and autoscaler heuristics.
